title: Repair a Handler and Activate Configuration
objectives: Repair a Handler and Activate Configuration
Verify state independently and preserve the source/deployment boundary.

tasks.instruction: Use the isolated Lab attempt. Open Terminal: ssh svc_ansible@ansible01 then cd ~/splunk-automation. V7 source additions are precommitted for this lesson; free practice can add them in Automation Operations. Commands and services are simulated.

The input task notifies an undefined handler. Correct the notification in roles/v7_inputs/tasks/main.yml to v7 restart splunk. Run the input playbook on ds01. Verify a single matching handler run and the effective input after activation.
Use the run output and independent configuration inspection to answer the evidence question. The source and operational checks must also pass.

hints: Inspect source, target scope and the latest run before retrying.
Use --limit ds01 and inspect btool after an actual apply.

references.purpose: Handlers run on change in definition order

checks.label: Running input matches the requested sourcetype

questions.prompt: Which handler activated the changed input?

setup.text:
- name: Create the managed input app
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: "{{ splunk_home }}/etc/apps/v7_practice/local"
    state: directory
    owner: splunk
    group: splunk
    mode: "0750"
- name: Supply the explicit teaching log
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    src: automation.log
    dest: "{{ practice_source }}"
    owner: splunk
    group: splunk
    mode: "0640"
- name: Render the monitored input
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: inputs.conf.j2
    dest: "{{ splunk_home }}/etc/apps/v7_practice/local/inputs.conf"
    owner: splunk
    group: splunk
    mode: "0640"
  notify: missing restart

feedback.success: Verified actual source, scoped execution and target state.
feedback.incomplete: Check the latest scoped run, source revision, ownership and activation. An answer or command text alone is insufficient.
